hadith:
Rubbing hands and feet with dust (Tayammum) - Narrated `Abdur Rahman bin Abza:

`Ammar said to `Umar "I rolled myself in the dust and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) who said, 'Passing dusted hands over the face and the backs of the hands is sufficient for you.' "
message: When Allah provides for our needs, we should respond with gratitude and compassion—never oppressing the orphan or turning away the beggar, for such kindness reflects our submission to His will. Remember that Allah humbles those who reject His guidance, while He honors those who follow His commands with sincerity and care for others. Let us strive to be among those who recognize Allah's blessings and share them generously with the vulnerable around us.
name:
Al Mudhil - المُذِلُّ - The Humiliator

Al Mudhil refers to Allah's attribute of causing disgrace or humiliation to those who oppose His commands or reject His guidance. This name emphasizes the power of Allah to elevate or debase individuals based on their actions and faith. It serves as a reminder of the consequences of turning away from righteousness and the importance of adhering to divine guidance.
verse:
Ad-Duhaa - The Morning Hours - 93:8-10

And did He not find you needy then satisfied your needs?

So do not oppress the orphan, nor repulse the beggar.
